# hamexam

**Practice tests for the United States amateur radio licence exams**

- **Version recorded:** 1.11.2
- **Categories:** `exams`
- **Upstream:** <https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/hamexam>

## What it does

Presents randomly drawn questions from the FCC amateur radio question pools -- Technician, General and Extra -- in the same proportions the real exam uses, marks the result, and tracks which subelements you are weak in.

## Why you would want it

The US exams are drawn verbatim from published pools, so practising against the pool is not a shortcut, it is the intended method. Working through them offline, without an account or a subscription, is what this offers.

## Before it will work

None. It is a study tool with no radio involved.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`morse`](../profiles/morse.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install hamexam --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `hamexam`

## Known problems

The question pool built into a package version is the pool at the time it was packaged. Pools are revised on a rolling cycle and Mint 22.3 carries 1.10.1 against 1.11.2 elsewhere (measured 2026-08-28) -- check the pool year against the current one before trusting a score. It covers the US exams only; `canadian-ham-exam` is the Canadian equivalent and other countries have neither.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
- The FCC question pools are revised on a rolling four-year cycle, one element at a time. A package version behind a pool revision is studying the wrong questions, which matters more here than a version gap usually does.
